sourceMaterialization.finding: The one-time read-only probe captured current OSM geometry around Ila/Grini and exact Kartverket address objects for Jøssingveien 33 and 31. The temporary workflow was removed after source capture.

officialHistory.finding: MiA documents that Grini fangeleir was established on 14 June 1941 in the original Ila women's-prison building. As the prisoner population grew, forest around the building was cleared and more than thirty barracks were built from 1942. MiA states that Ila fengsel og forvaringsanstalt occupies the original main building today.

historicalPlanControl.sourceName: Lokalhistoriewiki – Grini fangeleir and Griniboken camp plan
historicalPlanControl.finding: The wartime plan marks the original prison building as a masonry structure and shows the appeal area and expanded barracks compound around it. A 1945 appeal photograph is described as taken from the fourth floor of the original prison building toward the large appeal area. The source identifies the original building as today's Ila institution and places Fallskjermen inside it.

appliedBuilding.derivation: deterministic polygon centroid in lon*cos(meanLat),lat planar space
appliedBuilding.finding: The surviving original prison building is represented by a 41-node closed building polygon at the current Ila site. Its centroid provides a physically reproducible anchor for the documented historical camp core rather than a guessed perimeter centre.

addressCrossCheck.finding: The exact official address point for Ila lies approximately 23.5 metres from the applied building centroid. Kriminalomsorgen independently publishes the same visitor address for the current high-security prison.

interiorIdentityCrossCheck.name: Fallskjermen
interiorIdentityCrossCheck.finding: The mapped historical room lies inside building way 1420075236. Historical sources place Fallskjermen in the original prison building. OSM marks the room position as approximate, so it is identity QA only and not a production coordinate source.

museumVisitorAnchor.name: Grini museum
museumVisitorAnchor.finding: MiA states that the current museum occupies an authentic prisoner barrack moved after the war and now located just outside the original camp site. The museum is therefore retained as the public visitor anchor, not the canonical historical coordinate.

currentPrisonContext.name: Ila fengsel og forvaringsanstalt
currentPrisonContext.finding: The current secure-prison boundary surrounds the applied historical building anchor. It is operational access context only and is never used as historical camp geometry.

legacyCoordinate.finding: The provisional legacy point has no documented relationship to the original building, appeal area, barracks or preserved wartime features and is replaced.

historicalEntityCandidate.finding: The Wikidata point is geographically close to the historical core but remains unsuitable as a production coordinate because its coordinate statement has no cited derivation or feature role.

radiusDecision.finding: The radius increases to 360 metres so the inaccessible historical anchor, public museum visitor anchor and immediate documented camp-core landscape can function as one History Go place. The circle is deliberately not presented as the 1941–1945 perimeter.

accessDecision.finding: The canonical historical anchor lies inside today's active high-security Ila prison. History Go must never instruct users to approach or cross the prison security perimeter. Public interpretation is routed through Grinimuseet and ordinary lawful public access.

decision.representationLimit: The marker is the surviving original prison building used as a stable historical camp-core anchor. It is not the centroid or perimeter of the full wartime barracks camp.
